newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 100 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 60 billion bolivar ($125 million) auction of 178-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 18.93 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 20 billion bolivars ($42 million) in 267-day bills with a 19.36 percent coupon, and another 20 billion bolivars of 356-day bills with a 19.81 percent coupon.
Some 40 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

At last week's 100 billion bolivar auction, 178-, 267- and 358-day notes carried 18.81, 19.24, and 19.70 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that rose gently at the short end of the curve to 18.93, 20.33 and 21.05 percent.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
